goal: The user stacks tasks and has an AI work on them, the work resumes once the usage limit lifts, and the results are checked and taken in afterward. Once it's achieved, an AI stacks tasks and lets go, and afterward checks which tasks finished and which were given up, and takes their results in.

deliverable.name: The parts that run the stacked tasks, resume them after the limit, and report each task's end are drawn

decisions.decided: A queue stacked anew waits for the next time its start hour comes; a queue stacked again to carry on its unfinished tasks starts them at once.
The architecture says by which part and means a task that writes, such as one that runs its tests, writes only in its dir, as the README promises.

decisions.about: A runner that stops before its tasks end
decisions.decided: The architecture says how a queue whose runner stopped before its tasks ended, such as by a restart of the machine, is carried on to its end, and stacking it again is not refused for good.

lines: overnight carries each stacked task to its end without the user, so the user lets go after
- S1: the user wants each task they stack done in the hours they set, with no one there.
- S2: the user wants each finished task's whole result afterward, and why each other task ended
- P1.4: a queue is taken only once each task can start, so mistakes show while the user is there.
- Each run and reply written only by the record, which the stacker, the runner, and the checker
- P1: no one there while the tasks run
- P1.1: the tasks run apart from Claude Code, so they go on after the stacking session ends.
- P2.1: a task stopped by the usage limit goes on in its session two minutes after the reset.
- P3.2: a task given up for any reason stops no other task.
- runner (script)\
Carries each stacked task to its end without anyone.
- session (script)\
Runs a task's Claude Code session, and tells how it ended.
- commands (skill)\
- stacker (script)\
- Run\
Holds how far a task got: its session, its stops at the usage limit, and its end.
alt a task that can't start, such as a prompt that isn't there, a writing task that can't be held to its dir, or a queue whose runner still carries it [P1.3, P1.4]
else stopped by the limit the seventh time [P2.2]
else stopped by the limit an earlier time [P2.1]
